tae: A Tae”—addressing the mother—“can you believe that I would harm one hair of your baby’s head?”
Leading the rushing crowd was Chee Ping the First; in the midst panted A Tae and her white woman friend, and in the wake of all calmly and quietly pattered Little Me.
Miss McLeod did her best, and after a while Chee A Tae sat up and listened with some hope for her husband’s footsteps.
Then spake A Tae: “Teacher, forgive me,” besought she.
Chee A Tae was bitterly disappointed at seeing her husband without the babe.
